articles.title: Occupational hazards in hip and knee adult reconstruction surgery : a systematic review of physical and psychological stressors.
articles.authors: Innocenti M, Civinini R, Leggieri F, Lustig S, Batailler C, van Laarhoven SN, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of occupational hazards in surgery
articles.population: Adult reconstruction surgeons performing hip and knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Work-related injury prevalence, hearing loss rates, noise exposure levels, physiological demands (heart rate and energy expenditure), ergonomic strain, and impact of robotic-assisted surgery
articles.take_home: Surgeons performing hip and knee joint replacements face high rates of work-related injuries (66-96.5%), with nearly three times higher hearing loss compared to non-surgical doctors, significant physical strain, and high noise levels from the procedures. Robotic assistance can help with some physical demands but increases operating time and noise.

articles.title: More Technology, but Similar Early Safety: Robotic Versus Conventional Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty, a 30-Day Outcome National Database Study.
articles.authors: Sribhashyam S, Gooch BR, Yazdanpanah S, Setliff JC, Cassidy BP, Reiter CR, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA)
articles.sample_size: 727 robotic UKA and 1,454 conventional UKA cases
articles.outcomes: 30-day adverse events, major and minor complications, infectious complications, operative time, length of stay, outpatient rate
articles.take_home: Robotic-assisted knee surgery took longer but patients went home sooner and were more often treated as outpatients. Both robotic and conventional approaches had similar rates of complications in the first 30 days after surgery.

articles.title: Femoral Shortening Osteotomy Techniques in Total Hip Arthroplasty for Hartofilakidis Type C Developmental Hip Dysplasia: A 25-Year Single-Surgeon Series.
articles.authors: Macheras G, Argyrou C, Tzefronis D, Milaras C, Kostakos T, Nayar SK
articles.population: Patients with Hartofilakidis type C developmental hip dysplasia undergoing total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Bone healing at osteotomy site, leg-length restoration, rotational alignment, and nerve complications
articles.take_home: All femoral bones healed successfully after shortening surgery, with transverse subtrochanteric osteotomy providing the most reliable results. Three patients had temporary nerve problems that resolved within six months, and all patients achieved leg-length correction within five millimetres.

articles.title: Failure Rates After Treatment of Periprosthetic Joint Infection Using Musculoskeletal Infection Society Outcome Reporting Tool, Delphi, and Clinical Outcome Definitions.
articles.authors: Tyler JR, Grayson W, Wozniak A, Schmitt D, Brown NM
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic joint infection (infection around hip or knee implants) treated at a single academic medical centre
articles.outcomes: Failure rates at 12 months using three different definitions: MSIS-ORT (43.5%), Delphi criteria (40.8%), and clinical definition (47.3%)
articles.take_home: Treatment failure rates for joint infections around hip and knee implants vary depending on which definition is used, ranging from 41% to 47%. Different outcome definitions do not always classify individual patients the same way, which affects how we interpret whether treatment has been successful.

articles.title: Comparison of 90-Day Complications Between Direct Anterior and Postero-Lateral Total Hip Arthroplasty in Morbidly Obese Patients.
articles.authors: Bauer JA, Birbara B, Grosso MJ
articles.population: Morbidly obese and non-morbidly obese patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 5,933 primary THAs; 365 morbidly obese patients (238 direct anterior, 127 postero-lateral)
articles.outcomes: 90-day complications including periprosthetic fracture, revision surgery, operative time, and overall complication rates
articles.take_home: In morbidly obese patients having hip replacement, the direct anterior approach was quicker and had lower revision surgery rates, but overall complication risks were similar between both surgical approaches at 90 days. Both approaches appear safe to use in this patient group.

articles.title: Conversion Total Knee Arthroplasty After Tibial Plateau Fracture Open Reduction and Internal Fixation: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of 90-Day and One- and Three-Year Outcomes.
articles.authors: Luo Y, Soriano K, Strok M, Scolaro JA, Yang S, Hsiue P
articles.study_type: Propensity-matched observational cohort study using national database
articles.population: Adults aged 18 and over undergoing knee replacement after tibial plateau fracture surgery or as a primary procedure
articles.sample_size: 613 patients with prior fracture surgery matched to 613 primary knee replacement patients
articles.outcomes: Infection around the implant, need for revision surgery, stiffness requiring manipulation under anaesthesia, and hospital readmission within 30 days
articles.take_home: Patients who need knee replacement after a previous shin bone fracture have a higher risk of infection and needing further surgery compared with those having primary knee replacement. The risk appears to come from both the original fracture damage and any metal hardware left in place from the previous surgery.

articles.title: Fixed-loop and adjustable-loop femoral fixation provide comparable outcomes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A meta-analysis of comparative studies.
articles.authors: D'Ambrosi R, Patt T, Sundararajan SR, Sconfienza LM, Cristiani R, Smigielski R, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: International Knee Documentation Committee score, Lysholm score, Tegner Activity Scale, KT-1000 arthrometer measurements, Lachman and pivot-shift test grades, graft failure rates, reoperation rates
articles.take_home: Both types of femoral fixation in ACL reconstruction produce similar patient satisfaction, function, and knee stability outcomes. Although adjustable-loop fixation showed slightly better results in one physical examination test, this did not lead to better overall results for patients.

articles.title: Patellofemoral outcomes after kinematic versus mechanical alignment in primary total knee arthroplasty : a focused scoping review of head-to-head comparative studies.
articles.authors: Toyooka S, Osaki Y, Arai N, Kawano H, Nakagawa T
articles.study_type: Focused scoping review of head-to-head comparative studies
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Patellofemoral symptoms and patient-reported outcomes, patellofemoral-related interventions and complications, patellofemoral imaging and radiological measures
articles.take_home: Current evidence does not show that kinematic alignment causes more patellofemoral problems than mechanical alignment in knee replacement surgery, though the review identifies significant gaps in how these outcomes have been studied and reported.

articles.title: Incidence of Postoperative Patellar Crepitus in Total Knee Arthroplasty with Unresurfaced Patellae in Cruciate-Retaining and Posterior-Stabilized Designs.
articles.authors: Barton K, Aprey N, Hemmerle M, Behun MA, Bryman JA, Salimi M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty with unresurfaced patellae
articles.outcomes: Incidence of patellar crepitus (clicking or crackling sensation), comparison between posterior-stabilised and cruciate-retaining designs, need for reoperation, patient-reported outcomes
articles.take_home: About one in ten patients experienced patellar crepitus after knee replacement with unresurfaced kneecaps, with posterior-stabilised implants more likely to develop this than cruciate-retaining designs. Most patients with crepitus had no pain and only a small number needed further surgery.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence Systems in Early Prediction of Dislocation and Aseptic Loosening After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Abul MS, Sevim OF, Kilic NC, Agir M, Tuncay I
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 1,045 patients (34 with dislocation, 22 with aseptic loosening, 989 without complications)
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence systems in predicting dislocation and aseptic loosening on first-day postoperative radiographs, measured by sensitivity, specificity and area under the curve
articles.take_home: One artificial intelligence system showed good accuracy (91% for dislocation risk, 90% for loosening risk) in analysing hip replacement X-rays taken on the first day after surgery to predict future problems. The results were reproducible when the analysis was repeated.

articles.title: Sensor-Based Gait Recovery Analysis After Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A One-Year Follow-Up Study Integrating Muscle Strength and Patient-Reported Outcomes.
articles.authors: Chen WC, Wang CL, Lee SH, Peng SH, Chang CH, Hu CC, et al.
articles.population: Elderly patients aged 70 years or older with severe osteoarthritis undergoing total hip or knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Gait symmetry and speed, muscle strength, and patient-reported symptoms measured over one year using sensors, strength testing, and outcome questionnaires
articles.take_home: Patients showed good recovery after hip and knee replacement within a year, with muscle strength before surgery being the main factor predicting how well they walked afterwards, rather than how severe their arthritis was on X-rays. About 94% of hip and 92% of knee patients reported acceptable symptom improvement by 12 months.

articles.title: Task-specific determinants of one-year performance after unilateral primary total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Saiki Y, Kubo N, Ojima T
articles.population: Patients one year after primary unilateral total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Walking speed (40 m fast-paced walk test), sit-to-stand ability (30 second chair stand test), and stair climbing performance (11-step stair-climbing test)
articles.take_home: Strength in both legs, particularly the thigh muscles, was the most important factor affecting how well patients could walk, stand up from a chair, and climb stairs one year after knee replacement. Age also mattered, and for stair climbing, pain control and knee bending ability were additionally important.

articles.title: Bicruciate-stabilized total knee arthroplasty shows kinematics closer to the native knee than cruciate-substituting total knee arthroplasty: a cadaveric study using the Journey II system.
articles.authors: Shigekiyo S, Wada K, Hamada D, Tamaki Y, Sugimine Y, Tomita K, et al.
articles.population: Fresh-frozen cadaveric knees with intact anterior cruciate ligaments
articles.outcomes: Femoral rotation and anteroposterior translation during passive knee flexion, assessed using robotic-assisted navigation
articles.take_home: Bicruciate-stabilized knee replacements moved more like natural knees during bending than cruciate-substituting replacements, particularly in the way the knee translated forwards and backwards. However, neither type fully matched the natural knee's rotation patterns when first bending.

articles.title: Descriptive MRI-based morphometry of pediatric knee bony anatomy: cross-sectional age-related patterns of patellofemoral and tibiofemoral measures.
articles.authors: Scheible A, Ryland J, Magoline JA, Oravec M, Smith K, Madaan P, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 1-18 years without knee structural pathology
articles.outcomes: Measurements of knee bone dimensions including tibial tubercle-trochlear groove distance, trochlear depth, intercondylar notch width, tibial eminence morphology, posterior tibial slope, and lateral compartment morphometry, assessed for associations with age, sex, height, and BMI
articles.take_home: Absolute measurements of children's knee bones increase substantially as they grow taller, but certain commonly used measurement ratios remain relatively stable throughout childhood. These findings help doctors interpret knee imaging and plan surgery in children, but should be considered alongside soft-tissue and clinical factors rather than as the sole basis for identifying problems.

articles.title: Proximal femoral replacement for non-oncologic reconstruction: functional outcomes and survivorship in 30 patients.
articles.authors: Bodu Lamberti EM, Monclou G, Karduss Preciado C
articles.population: Patients undergoing proximal femoral replacement for non-oncologic indications (such as trauma or infection)
articles.outcomes: Modified Harris Hip Score, infection-free survival, revision-free arthroplasty survival, complications
articles.take_home: Proximal femoral replacement for non-cancer bone loss resulted in modest functional recovery with a mean score of 54 out of 100, but half of patients experienced complications including infection. The procedure preserved limbs in most cases, though longer-term survival rates decreased over five years.

articles.title: Manual versus robotic-assisted revision total knee arthroplasty for instability : a one-year cohort analysis.
articles.authors: Burbelo A, Stone W, Clark T, Huffman AB, Murphy A, Potts CE, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee arthroplasty for instability
articles.outcomes: Operating time, length of stay, joint line change, posterior condylar offset change, 30- and 90-day complications, KOOS-JR score, range of motion at three months and one year, one-year reoperation-free survival
articles.take_home: Robotic-assisted revision knee surgery achieved better restoration of the knee's offset alignment compared to manual surgery, but took longer to perform. Both approaches had similar complication rates, hospital stays, pain and function scores, and one-year survival rates.

articles.title: Preservation of periprosthetic bone with a collum-fixated short stem versus conventional metaphyseal-fixated stems in total hip arthroplasty: a randomized controlled trial with 2-year follow-up in 61 patients.
articles.authors: Tjonneland A, Christiansen JD, Jakobsen T, Nielsen PT
articles.population: Adults with primary osteoarthritis of the hip undergoing total hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Bone mineral density in the hip bone around the implant at 24 months; patient-reported outcomes including quality of life, hip function and joint awareness
articles.take_home: A shorter, collar-fixed hip implant design (Primoris) preserved more bone around the implant than a standard longer implant (Echo) after 2 years, with no difference in how well patients felt their hip was working. Better bone preservation may be helpful if patients need revision surgery in future.

articles.title: The Swedish experience of capital realignment surgery for slipped capital femoral epiphysis: results from a nationwide retrospective cohort of 28 patients.
articles.authors: Nilsson J, Lindell M, Ortegren J, Herngren B, Stenmarker M, Michno P, et al.
articles.population: Patients with slipped capital femoral epiphysis treated with capital realignment surgery
articles.outcomes: Avascular necrosis of femoral head, Copenhagen Hip and Groin Outcome Score (HAGOS), and 12-item International Hip Outcome Tool (iHOT12)
articles.take_home: About 1 in 5 patients developed avascular necrosis after capital realignment surgery for slipped capital femoral epiphysis. Outcomes were better when surgery was done soon after diagnosis and when blood flow to the femoral head was monitored during the operation.

articles.title: The Impact of Lesser Tuberosity Osteotomy Repair After Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Aleem AW, Zmistowski BM, Sefko J, Chen L, Keener JD
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty with intact subscapularis suitable for reattachment
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) score, internal rotation range of motion, internal rotation functional score, active shoulder motions in other planes
articles.take_home: Repairing the subscapularis tendon during reverse shoulder replacement surgery led to better shoulder function scores and improved ability to rotate the arm inward at 2 years, without reducing movement in other directions.

articles.title: Outcomes of Total Knee Arthroplasty in Patients Receiving Chronic Antithrombotic Therapy: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Vosoughi F, Ramezanpour MR, Hashemi FS, Kazemivand S, Dorcheh SS, Oskouei IM
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty who were taking long-term blood-thinning medications
articles.sample_size: 17 studies; 104,182 patients on blood-thinners and 261,139 control patients
articles.outcomes: Blood loss, transfusion rates, hospital stay length, infection, wound problems, blood clots, heart attacks, lung clots, and revision surgery
articles.take_home: Patients taking warfarin had more bleeding, needed more transfusions and longer hospital stays than those on other blood-thinners, but direct oral anticoagulants actually had lower infection rates. Total knee replacement can be done safely in patients on blood-thinning medications with proper care, though warfarin patients need closer monitoring.

articles.title: Modular Fluted Tapered Stems in Periprosthetic Femoral Fractures: Curved Stems are Protective Against Intraoperative Fracture and Postoperative Subsidence.
articles.authors: Park CW, Chang Jang M, Jeong SJ, Cho K, Lim SJ, Park YS
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision hip arthroplasty for periprosthetic femoral fractures
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative fracture occurrence, stem subsidence, Harris Hip Score, implant survivorship free of re-revision surgery at 10 years
articles.take_home: Curved stems were better than straight stems at reducing the risk of fractures during surgery and stem movement after surgery. Most patients had good hip function and 94.6% of implants remained in place without needing further surgery over 10 years.

articles.title: Risk Factor Analysis of Delayed Union or Nonunion After Total Hip Arthroplasty Combined with Subtrochanteric Transverse Osteotomy in Patients Who have Crowe Type IV Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip.
articles.authors: Li H, Li M, Zhang B, Xie H, Ling H, Liu Y, et al.
articles.population: Patients with Crowe type IV developmental dysplasia of the hip undergoing total hip arthroplasty combined with subtrochanteric transverse osteotomy
articles.outcomes: Delayed union or nonunion at the osteotomy site; radiographic parameters including canal fill ratios and cortical apposition ratios
articles.take_home: Delayed union or nonunion occurred in 19.2% of cases overall, but was significantly less common when autogenous bone plate wiring was used (13.8%) compared to stem press-fit fixation alone (36.1%). Poor bone-to-implant contact at the osteotomy site increased the risk of healing problems.

articles.title: Reduced compression time is not sufficient for stability in patellar buttons.
articles.authors: Bauer L, Gramzow J, Brensing M, Bartz B, Woiczinski M, Matziolis G
articles.population: Human patellae from cadavers
articles.outcomes: Cement morphology, micromotion during cyclic loading, maximum shear force at failure
articles.take_home: Shortening the time that a surgeon applies pressure to a patellar button during knee replacement surgery led to more movement at the cement-bone interface, even though the final strength was similar. This suggests that maintaining full compression time during cement hardening is important for early stability of the implant.

articles.title: Absolute knee extensor strength, not limb symmetry, predicts outcomes and defines a rehabilitation threshold after medial opening-wedge high tibial osteotomy.
articles.authors: Lee DW, Kim RJ, Beak JY, Lee WII, Jung JW, Lee NK, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with receiver operating characteristic analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial opening-wedge high tibial osteotomy for knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 125 patients at baseline, 90 at mid-term follow-up (mean 37.2 months)
articles.outcomes: Knee extensor and flexor strength, International Knee Documentation Committee subjective score, Y-Balance Test, patient-reported outcomes
articles.take_home: After knee osteotomy surgery, achieving a knee extensor strength of at least 1.3 newtons per kilogram of body weight was associated with better patient satisfaction and function. Absolute strength of the operated leg was more important for overall satisfaction than how equally strong both legs were compared to each other.

articles.title: Promises and limitations of deep learning for predicting knee osteoarthritis progression from medical imaging: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Gillani A, von Eisenhart-Rothe R, Woertler K, Hirschmann MT, Rueckert D, Hinterwimmer F
articles.study_type: Systematic review of deep learning studies
articles.population: Patients with knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 33 studies included; individual studies ranged from 340 to 52,981 knees (median 4298)
articles.outcomes: Predictive accuracy of deep learning models for knee osteoarthritis progression measured by area under receiver operating characteristic curve; models assessed for structural deterioration, symptomatic worsening, or surgical intervention
articles.take_home: Deep learning models show promise for predicting knee osteoarthritis progression, with some performing well in research settings, but most have not been properly tested on new patient groups outside the original studies, and they need more rigorous development before they could be used in NHS clinics.

articles.title: Reduced patella medialization in valgus and varus knees using a KA-optimized femoral component in kinematically aligned TKA.
articles.authors: Simon JM, Siedow TM, Thorwachter C, Traxler H, Kirchhoff K, Endres F, et al.
articles.population: Fresh-frozen cadaveric knees with valgus and varus alignment
articles.outcomes: Patellofemoral kinematics, contact area, peak pressure patterns and quadriceps force with kinematically aligned versus standard femoral components
articles.take_home: A kinematically aligned femoral component reduced unwanted inward movement of the kneecap compared to standard designs in both bowlegged and knock-kneed knees, but did not reduce pressure on the kneecap joint or improve muscle function.

articles.title: Association between tibiofemoral bone and meniscus morphology and dynamic tibiofemoral movements during jump-landing tasks in patients following ACL reconstruction.
articles.authors: Vendrig T, Brouwer RW, Hoogeslag RAG, Houdijk H, Olde Heuvel J, de Vries AJ, et al.
articles.study_type: Cross-sectional observational study with regression analysis
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Association between knee bone and meniscus shape (measured on MRI before surgery) and knee movement patterns (anterior tibial translation and internal tibial rotation) during jumping and hopping tasks
articles.take_home: Certain knee bone shapes were linked to greater internal rotation of the tibia during landing, which may help identify patients who could benefit from additional surgery such as anterolateral corner reconstruction. However, bone-shaping surgery (tibial osteotomy) may not be helpful for most patients based on these findings.

articles.title: Management of increased posterior tibial slope in ACL deficiency: A narrative review and recommendation of the Osteotomy Committee of the German Knee Society.
articles.authors: Mayer P, Furmetz J, Bode G, Angele P, Ahrend MD, Leutheuser S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with anterior cruciate ligament deficiency and increased posterior tibial slope
articles.outcomes: Recommendations for measuring posterior tibial slope, surgical indications for correction, and preferred surgical techniques
articles.take_home: Posterior tibial slope should be measured on specific X-ray views with careful attention to alignment. Whether surgery is needed depends on individual factors like how unstable the knee is and previous injuries, not just a single measurement number. An infratuberositary approach for surgical correction appears technically easier and safer than other methods.

articles.title: Impact of playing position on ACL injury characteristics, risk and career outcomes in football-An analysis of 742 cases of the ACL registry in German football.
articles.authors: Hasegawa S, Krutsch W, Koga H, Alt V, Szymski D, Huber L
articles.population: Male football players across professional, semi-professional and amateur levels in Germany
articles.outcomes: ACL injury rates by playing position, injury mechanisms, return-to-play over five seasons in professionals, and career outcomes within three seasons after injury
articles.take_home: Defenders and midfielders had the highest ACL injury rates during matches, whilst forwards showed the greatest career impact with nearly half dropping to a lower competitive level. Injury causes differed by level: professional forwards and defenders suffered mostly direct contact injuries, whereas amateur players experienced mainly non-contact injuries.

articles.title: Differences in cutting biomechanics between landing error scoring system risk groups among male collegiate athletes.
articles.authors: Tsai WC, Yeh HH, Yen KT, Chen ZR
articles.population: Male collegiate athletes
articles.outcomes: Hip, knee and ankle biomechanics during 20-degree cutting manoeuvres; vertical ground reaction force
articles.take_home: The Landing Error Scoring System can identify movement pattern differences during cutting as well as landing. Athletes at higher risk of ACL injury showed different knee and hip positioning during cutting compared to lower-risk athletes.

articles.title: Delayed anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction in skeletally immature patients is associated with increased prevalence and complexity of meniscal tears.
articles.authors: Rossi C, Alhalalmeh MI, Piussi R, Zaffagnini S, Grassi A
articles.population: Skeletally immature patients (mean age 14.4 years) undergoing primary ACL reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Prevalence and patterns of meniscal tears stratified by time between injury and surgery
articles.take_home: Waiting longer than 6 months for ACL surgery in young patients was linked with more damage to the inner knee cartilage (meniscus), particularly complex tears that are harder to repair. Having surgery within 3 months was associated with different, often less serious cartilage damage patterns.
